value.rationale: Signed unit-row-sum equilibration is central to algorithms for symmetric M-matrices and sometimes proposed as preconditioning. The proved dimension-order barrier shows that even with input Euclidean condition K held constant, the EXACT requested output must have condition Theta(d) and diagonal-spread Theta(sqrt(d)), sharply delimiting any expectation of dimension-free condition retention. A weighted star is a canonical sparse graph rather than an arbitrary unmotivated numeric slice, and the exact coefficient quantifies the practical tradeoff. No downstream theorem or runtime claim is assumed.
